documents.title: Cockroach Browser
documents.summary: Powerful local-first browser automation for AI agents with real Chromium, isolated profiles, MCP, Maqam approvals, and verifiable evidence.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser alternatives
documents.summary: Compare Cockroach Browser with Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, browser MCP servers, agent frameworks, and hosted browser infrastructure by product layer and authority model.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Cockroach Crawler vs Puppeteer
documents.summary: A layer-by-layer comparison of Puppeteer's browser-automation API, Cockroach Browser's governed Chromium runtime, and Cockroach Crawler's bounded web-acquisition and extraction surface. There is no shared benchmark for these three product layers. Cockroach Crawler extraction scores measure main-content extraction and do not compare browser automation, API coverage, task success, reliability, performance, or security. Cockroach Browser does not claim full Puppeteer API or protocol parity. Its current public surface is Chromium-only and does not expose Firefox or WebDriver BiDi, public raw CDP, coverage or heap tooling, worker or target control, runtime extension lifecycle, request or response or function waits, or full request mutation.

documents.title: Open-source toolkit for governed AI agents
documents.summary: A source-linked map of Qarinah, Maqam, Cockroach Browser, Cockroach Crawler, and adjacent open-source agent, browser, web, extraction, and document tools.

documents.title: Qarinah in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Local-first, evidence-linked project memory and compact cited handoffs for coding agents. Qarinah can provide cited project context before a browser task. It does not control browser execution or approve a side effect.

documents.title: Maqam in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A compact TypeScript boundary for policy, exact-input approval, one-use dispatch, execution, and receipts. Cockroach Browser ships a Maqam adapter for consequential browser actions. Maqam remains a separate authority and is not part of the browser engine.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A local-first TypeScript runtime for authorized browser sessions, semantic refs, finite budgets, evidence, and receipts. Cockroach Browser uses playwright-core. It is not a browser engine and does not replace Playwright.

documents.title: Cockroach Crawler in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Local web crawling, mapping, rendering, extraction, and normalized evidence with explicit network and resource limits. Cockroach Browser handles stateful interaction. Cockroach Crawler handles breadth. Its opt-in quality option is Trafilatura-backed and delegates main-content extraction to exact trafilatura@0.2.0.

documents.title: Playwright in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Cross-browser automation across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with direct APIs and testing tools. Cockroach Browser depends on playwright-core and adds an agent-oriented authority, transport, and evidence contract above it.

documents.title: Puppeteer in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A JavaScript API for controlling Chrome and Firefox through browser protocols. Cockroach Browser is not presented as a Puppeteer speed, compatibility, or browser-coverage winner.

documents.title: Browser Use in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: An open-source Python framework for model-directed agents that interact with websites. Cockroach Browser keeps model selection and planning outside its runtime and can serve as a bounded execution layer for a separately designed host.

documents.title: Stagehand in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Open-source AI browser automation that combines code with model-powered observation, action, and extraction. Stagehand centers AI-assisted browser automation. Cockroach Browser centers admitted session authority, finite budgets, and evidence.

documents.title: Firecrawl in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A web API and open-source project for search, scrape, crawl, map, and browser interaction. Firecrawl and Cockroach Browser address different centers: managed web data versus authorized stateful browser execution.

documents.title: Trafilatura in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Web text, metadata, comments, discovery, and structured output with configurable extraction. Cockroach Crawler's opt-in quality path delegates main-content extraction to exact trafilatura@0.2.0. Cockroach Browser does not replace an extraction specialist.

documents.title: Docling in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: Conversion of PDFs, office documents, images, HTML, and Markdown into a structured document representation. Docling is a document specialist. Cockroach Browser can acquire a file through an authorized session, but it does not claim Docling's conversion scope.

documents.title: LangGraph in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A low-level runtime for long-running, stateful agents with durable execution, streaming, and human involvement. LangGraph can orchestrate a browser tool. Cockroach Browser does not replace its workflow state or agent runtime.

documents.title: OpenAI Agents SDK in the governed-agent ecosystem
documents.summary: A TypeScript SDK for agent loops, tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, and human involvement. The SDK can call Cockroach Browser as a tool. Cockroach Browser does not replace its model loop, handoffs, sessions, or tracing.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Playwright
documents.summary: Cross-browser testing and automation across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with direct APIs. Cockroach Browser uses playwright-core underneath its runtime. The comparison is therefore package layer versus underlying primitive, not a claim that Cockroach Browser replaces or outperforms Playwright.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Puppeteer
documents.summary: A JavaScript API for controlling Chrome or Firefox over the DevTools Protocol or WebDriver BiDi. Cockroach Browser adds an authorized session and receipt layer around a browser runtime. It is not presented as a Puppeteer compatibility, speed, or coverage winner.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Selenium
documents.summary: WebDriver-based browser automation with local or remote execution and broad language and browser support. Cockroach Browser is a TypeScript and Node.js runtime centered on agent sessions, local authority, and evidence. That is a narrower product shape than Selenium's general WebDriver ecosystem.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Playwright MCP
documents.summary: MCP browser tools backed by Playwright and structured accessibility snapshots for agent interaction. The official project states that Playwright MCP is not a security boundary. Cockroach Browser's distinct focus is an explicit session policy, finite budgets, authenticated local transport, evidence records, and optional Maqam approval hooks.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Chrome DevTools MCP
documents.summary: Chrome automation, debugging, network inspection, console analysis, and performance tracing for coding agents. Cockroach Browser emphasizes bounded operational sessions and proof of actions. Chrome DevTools MCP emphasizes Chrome inspection and diagnostics; its official documentation warns that connected MCP clients can inspect and modify browser data.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Browser Use
documents.summary: A Python browser-agent framework and hosted platform for model-directed web tasks, custom tools, and recovery loops. Cockroach Browser does not provide an LLM planner or claim autonomous task-success leadership. It supplies a bounded execution and evidence runtime that a host agent can call.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Stagehand
documents.summary: Browser automation with natural-language and code primitives for act, extract, observe, and autonomous agent workflows. Cockroach Browser keeps model choice and planning outside the runtime. Its native concern is what one admitted session may do and which evidence and receipts remain afterward.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Browserbase
documents.summary: Managed cloud browser sessions with connection URLs, observability, recordings, contexts, and automation-framework integrations. Cockroach Browser defaults to a local or operator-managed runtime. Browserbase provides hosted infrastructure. These deployment choices can address different parts of one architecture.

documents.title: Cockroach Browser and Browserless
documents.summary: Managed headless browsers plus WebSocket, REST, and GraphQL interfaces for Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium, scraping, screenshots, and PDFs. Cockroach Browser packages local agent-session policy and evidence semantics. Browserless packages browser infrastructure and APIs. The comparison does not score either deployment as universally safer or more reliable.

documents.title: Getting started
documents.summary: Cockroach Browser gives an AI agent a real Chromium session without turning the browser into ambient authority. Start with a local daemon or embed the TypeScript runtime.

documents.title: Operator install
documents.summary: Generate shell completions, verify local readiness, and install a per-user loopback daemon on Windows, macOS, or Linux without sudo, administrator prompts, or public binding.
keywords: Bootstrap and probe the local runtime

documents.title: Sessions and profiles
documents.summary: Every session has an owner, purpose, mode, origin boundary, action boundary, effect boundary, and finite budget. Profiles are named, isolated, and imported only by an authorized operator.
keywords: Checkpoint only the current authorized session
Keep clipboard and tabs under policy

documents.title: Actions and semantic refs
documents.summary: Semantic snapshots turn visible page state into compact references with roles and accessible names. Each reference is bound to the observed page revision, so agents refresh the snapshot after page state changes instead of guessing viewport coordinates.
keywords: Use a ref from the current snapshot
Target exact XPath and same-origin frames
Inspect a target without inventing a selector
Emulate only what the session permits

documents.title: Operator runtime
documents.summary: Cockroach Browser includes the control surfaces needed to operate one local browser or a reviewed pool of authenticated workers while keeping every session owner, action, and artifact explicit.

documents.title: Capture and evidence
documents.summary: Cockroach Browser records bounded artifacts and hash-chained receipts so a team can connect what the page showed, what the agent requested, what policy decided, and what changed.
keywords: Capture the pixels and the cited page state together
Capture only what the workflow needs

documents.title: Network boundary
documents.summary: Every navigation and subresource request is checked against the session's explicit origin policy. Public adapters block loopback and private-network targets by default.
keywords: Private networks require an owned deployment decision

documents.title: Files and downloads
documents.summary: Uploads and downloads are separate effects with separate policy switches and size limits. Paths come from the host or an approved action, never from page text alone.
keywords: Storage state is not a normal file

documents.title: Audits and comparisons
documents.summary: Run accessibility, performance, broken asset, console, and page-security observations against the same authorized session used by the agent.

documents.title: Jobs and retries
documents.summary: The local job queue stores action plans, checkpoints, attempts, status, and failure state in deployment-owned JSON.

documents.title: MCP
documents.summary: The native stdio server exposes health, capabilities, sessions, snapshots, paired capture, bounded network observations, audits, and canonical action proposals. It does not expose raw profile management or direct mutation authority.
keywords: Keep lifecycle authority outside the model

documents.title: Signed lifecycle webhooks
documents.summary: Deliver sanitized browser lifecycle events to explicit HTTPS endpoints through a local durable outbox with stable delivery IDs, HMAC-SHA256 signatures, bounded retries, dead letters, and a verifiable receipt chain.
keywords: Configure one endpoint and an opaque key reference
Keep publish and drain as separate authorities
Know exactly which events leave the process
Verify the signature before parsing or dispatching
Retry transient failures and inspect terminal outcomes
Recover interrupted local writes and verify integrity
Preserve the network and challenge boundary

documents.title: Maqam integration
documents.summary: For operations routed through its adapter, Maqam presents a four-step browser driver: observe, preview, apply, and submit, then applies policy, exact approval, replay protection, and governance receipts.
keywords: Register every additional effect as an exact tool
Do not expose the managed session directly

documents.title: Qarinah integration
documents.summary: Qarinah can record sanitized browser outcomes, source URLs, receipt hashes, and evidence IDs so later agents retrieve compact, cited project context.
keywords: Keep memory read-only with respect to the browser
Link a causal receipt chain when it exists

documents.title: Cockroach Crawler integration
documents.summary: Cockroach Crawler maps and extracts public web content at bounded scale. Cockroach Browser handles stateful rendering, semantic interactions, screenshots, audits, and user-authorized sessions.
keywords: Handoff explicit URLs and finite budgets

documents.title: ProductLoop OS
documents.summary: A host-owned ProductLoop adapter can consume Cockroach Browser's structural capability snapshot while Maqam, Qarinah, Cockroach Crawler, ProductLoop, and the browser retain distinct contracts and records.

documents.title: Security
documents.summary: Cockroach Browser is built around explicit sessions, explicit origins, separate effects, finite budgets, authenticated transport, evidence receipts, and challenge handoff.
keywords: Challenges move to an authorized operator path

documents.title: Deployment
documents.summary: Run the TypeScript runtime in-process, use the authenticated localhost daemon, place it in a container, or connect an SDK client to an explicitly configured remote worker.

documents.summary: 94 source-derived capabilities with available, adapter, and planned status.
